milestones.title: Movement Plotting (Complete)
milestones.vision: Deliver the complete movement plotting and resolution loop — UI, server rules, and visual playback — so a player can fight test_fleet.json indefinitely with every documented movement rule enforced.
success_criteria: Player can load test_fleet.json, plot every player-0 ship via the Movement button, see MA / path / tacking probability live, and submit per-ship plots
End Planning advances the phase only when every player-0 ship has a submitted plot; re-plotting allowed before End Planning is pressed
Stub-AI plots all non-player ships through the real plotting protocol before MOVEMENT_RESOLUTION begins, with Trace logs confirming strategy and decisions
MOVEMENT_RESOLUTION runs impulse-by-impulse via MovementResolver and produces a complete ResolutionLog
Playback animates ships hex-by-hex; contested-hex and bear-off prompts pause playback and accept the player's choice; tacking failures, collisions, and fouling all observable
After playback, ships are at resolved positions with updated facing and speed; plotted_actions.movement cleared; loop sustains 5+ turns with no console errors
All unit tests, 12 scenario integration fixtures, and the determinism test pass via `make test`; no regression in existing tests

key_risks.risk: Mock MovementValidator full rewrite — 12+ interlocking rules over five JSON tables surface bugs only in real play
key_risks.whyItMatters: If a rule interaction is wrong, plots are illegal under the real game and the resolver gets garbage input

key_risks.risk: Impulse-by-impulse contested-hex correctness with 3+ ships, off-map bear-off, and simultaneous collisions
key_risks.whyItMatters: Fleet engagements depend on this math being right; ambiguity here corrupts every multi-ship resolution
Existing env tests must still pass; silent drift here would invalidate the determinism contract

key_risks.risk: Async/await on UI prompts during simulation is a new pattern in this codebase
key_risks.whyItMatters: Deadlocks here would freeze the entire MOVEMENT_RESOLUTION phase

key_risks.risk: is_tacking_attempt flag must remain authoritative across every plot edit and undo
key_risks.whyItMatters: Wrong probability shown to the player undermines a key tactical UX moment

proof_strategy.whatWillBeProven: All single-ship rule fixtures pass at S03; 5-turn sustained playtest at S10 confirms real-play correctness
Two-ship head-on, three-ship contested, two-ship swap, off-map bear-off fixtures all green
Existing env tests pass; same seed reproduces the same wind sequence
Playback controller exercises the pattern end-to-end with stub-AI injected answers
Plot the tack pattern, then undo past trigger; flag must flip true→false correctly and the UI follows

milestones.verification_contract: Unit tests (test/unit/test_data_manager_bearing_off.gd, test_movement_validator_*.gd, test_movement_resolver_*.gd) prove rule math and table lookups. Integration tests under test/fixtures/scenarios/ prove the validator → resolver → state-update pipeline against 12 fixture scenarios. Determinism test proves identical seed + plots → identical ResolutionLog. All pass via `make test`. No regression in existing tests.
milestones.verification_integration: Loading test_fleet.json end-to-end, plotting the player fleet through the UI, watching stub-AI plots get rule-validated by the real protocol, observing MOVEMENT_RESOLUTION run impulse-by-impulse, and seeing playback animate ships into their resolved positions across 5+ turns of sustained play.
milestones.verification_operational: Five-turn sustained playtest of test_fleet.json with no console errors, no state drift between turns, no stale UI. Trace logs visible for every validator rule-block and every resolver event. Developer UI (F12) shows current-turn ResolutionLog for inspection.
milestones.verification_uat: Manual playthrough confirming: Movement button initiates plotting session; valid next hexes appear; MA / path / tacking probability shown live; undo/cancel/submit per ship work; End Planning gates on completion; playback animates and pauses for prompts; ships end at resolved positions with correct facing and speed.
definition_of_done: All 9 acceptance criteria from M001-CONTEXT.md observable in manual play of test_fleet.json
All unit and integration tests in test/unit/ and test/fixtures/scenarios/ pass via `make test`
5-turn sustained loop with no console errors
Trace logs visible for every validator rule-block and every resolver event
All M001 code paths covered by either unit or integration tests
No regression in existing tests (test_data_manager_*, test_trace)
milestones.requirement_coverage: Covers: R001, R002, R003, R004, R005, R006, R007, R008, R009, R010, R011, R012, R013, R014, R015, R016. milestones.boundary_map_markdown:
### S01 → S02

Produces:
- `DataManager.get_bearing_off_probability(crew_quality: String, maneuverability: String) -> float` with assert() validation
- `DataManager.load_scenario(...)` hard-errors on missing `seed` field; `seed:-1` → fresh seed (trace-logged)
- Loaded scenario dict carries validated `seed: int`
- crew_quality normalization: scenarios that say `"Trained"` map to a letter on load (or scenarios updated to use letters directly)
- `test/unit/test_data_manager_bearing_off.gd` exists and passes

Consumes:
- nothing (first slice)

### S02 → S03

Produces:
- `GameState.rng: RandomNumberGenerator` is the single seeded RNG
- `GameState.start_new_game(scenario_data)` seeds rng from scenario_data.seed
- `EnvironmentController` consumes `GameState.rng`; its own RNG removed
- Existing env tests still pass; same seed reproduces same wind sequence

Consumes:
- S01: validated scenario dict with `seed`

### S03 → S04

Produces:
- `MovementValidator` real rules (single-ship only): MA recalc per pivot, accel/decel bounds against last-turn speed, turning-table min-forward rule, pivot caps (max 2/turn + free pivot at MA=0), luffing, in-irons at plot start, fast-tack +1 MA bonus, map bounds
- `MovementPlottingSession` carries `pivots_used: int`, `forward_hexes_since_last_pivot: int`
- `PlotStep.move_type` populated by validator
- `Trace.trace_log("MovementValidator", ...)` on every rule-block
- Unit tests for the math + scenario fixtures for single-ship rules pass

Consumes:
- S02: `GameState.rng` available
- S01: `DataManager` wrappers and seed contract

### S03 → S05

Produces (hook into S05 work):
- Validator exposes `is_tacking_attempt(session_state) -> bool` (or equivalent computation hook)
- Session has `is_tacking_attempt: bool` field updated on every select_hex / undo

### S04 → S10

Produces:
- PLANNING UI fleet workflow: ship list, Movement button initiates plotting, valid-hex display, MA display, plotted-path display, undo/cancel/submit per ship
- End Planning button enabled only when all player-0 ships submitted
- Re-plotting allowed before End Planning
- Protocol responses < 50ms on local server

Consumes:
- S03: validator returns correct ValidNextHexes

### S05 → S06

Produces:
- `MovementPlottingSession.is_tacking_attempt` is authoritative across edits/undos
- UI shows live tacking probability from `tacking_table.json` + DRMs
- Validator marks session for tacking attempt; resolver reads the flag

Consumes:
- S03: validator hook + session fields
- S04: UI surface for the probability display

### S06 → S07

Produces:
- `MovementResolver.run(plotted_ships) -> ResolutionLog` for single-ship plots
- `ResolutionLog` data classes (per-impulse, per-ship event types) in MovementTypes
- Tacking success roll (from `tacking_table.json` + DRMs) made by resolver
- In-irons escape roll made by resolver

Consumes:

- S02: `GameState.rng`

### S07 → S09

Produces:
- `MovementResolver` multi-ship: impulse-by-impulse loop, contested-hex DRM math, surrender prompt event in log, bear-off prompt event in log, collisions, 50% fouling rule
- `ResolutionLog` schema final
- Multi-ship integration fixtures pass

Consumes:

### S08 → S10

Produces:
- `StubAI` (scripts/server/stub_ai.gd) drives the plotting protocol for every non-player ship at PLANNING start

Consumes:

### S09 → S10

Produces:

slices.title: S01
slices.demo: make test-file F=test/unit/test_data_manager_bearing_off.gd passes; loading a scenario without `seed` hard-errors; seed:-1 logs fresh-seed generation; crew_quality letter normalization complete.

This closes the slice's boundary contract to S02 (validated scenario dict carrying `seed: int`) and to S03+ (typed `get_bearing_off_probability(crew_quality, maneuverability) -> float` lookup with assert() validation). Per override D010 (2026-05-11), the slice exit bar is "all tests pass, even preexisting failures" — T03 fixes the preexisting failures and T04 is a clean-room verification gate.

- `make test-file F=test/unit/test_data_manager_bearing_off.gd` passes (new file, T01).
- `make test-file F=test/unit/test_data_manager_scenarios.gd` passes with new tests covering: seed honored, seed:-1 generates a fresh non-negative seed, missing seed hard-errors via push_error + zero-size return, crew_quality "Trained"/"Veteran"/"Elite"/"Green" all normalize to single letters in the returned dict (T02).
- `make clean && make test` passes overall with zero `Failing Tests` and zero `Errors`, from a clean `.godot` import cache (T04).
- `data/scenarios/test_basic.json` and `data/scenarios/test_fleet.json` both contain a top-level integer `seed` field; `_create_default_scenario()` returns `seed: -1`.
- `data/rules/bearing_off_table.json` exists, parses cleanly, and exercises every (crew_quality, maneuverability) cell tested by the unit test.

slices.proof_level: Contract — this slice proves DataManager rule-lookup boundary contracts (bearing-off lookup, seed contract, crew_quality normalization) via unit tests on the real JSON tables. No runtime/UI integration in this slice. Per override D010, the slice exit bar is enforced via `make clean && make test` from a clean import cache (T04).
slices.integration_closure: Upstream surfaces consumed: `scripts/autoload/data_manager.gd` (existing load_*_table / get_* pattern), `scripts/autoload/trace.gd` (used for seed:-1 log line). New wiring introduced: `bearing_off_table` loaded from a new JSON file; `load_scenario` now mutates the returned dict (seed resolution + crew_quality normalization). What remains before M001 is usable end-to-end: GameState must actually call `load_bearing_off_table()` at startup (deferred — first consumer in S06 will add the autoload line); GameState.rng seeded from the validated seed (S02); the validator + resolver themselves (S03/S06/S07).
slices.observability_impact: Runtime signals: `Trace.trace_log("ScenarioLoad", ...)` on each scenario load — logs the scenario name, the resolved seed value, and whether it came from JSON or was generated from `-1`. Failure visibility: missing-seed scenarios produce a `push_error` with the scenario name; the function returns `{}` so callers see a zero-size dict (matches existing failure shape). Inspection surfaces: F12 dev UI already surfaces Trace categories — ScenarioLoad will appear there automatically. Bearing-off loader prints `Loaded bearing off table with N crew quality grades` mirroring the existing load_*_table convention. Redaction constraints: none (no PII / secrets in scenario or rule data). Process-level artifact: `.gsd/runtime/s01_t04_clean_make_test.log` archives the clean-room green run for forensics.

tasks.title: Add bearing_off_table.json + DataManager wrapper + unit tests
tasks.description: Create `data/rules/bearing_off_table.json` keyed by crew_quality letter (A..G) → maneuverability letter (a..d) → float success probability (0.0..1.0). Probabilities derive from CA rules VI.D.2 (roll SK or more on d6 with class DRMs: -1 class 1, +0 class 2, +1 class 3, +2 class 4) using the mapping SK = numeric value of CQ letter (A=1..G=7) and maneuverability serving as a class proxy (a=class1..d=class4). Document the derivation in a top-level `_doc` field inside the JSON. Then in `scripts/autoload/data_manager.gd`: add `var bearing_off_table: Dictionary = {}`; add `func load_bearing_off_table(file_path: String = "res://data/rules/bearing_off_table.json") -> bool` mirroring the existing load_*_table funcs (push_warning + return false on missing, push_error on parse failure, store Dictionary on success); add `func get_bearing_off_probability(crew_quality: String, maneuverability: String) -> float` with assert() on both params (crew_quality A..G case-insensitive, maneuverability a..d case-insensitive), returning 0.0 on any missing key with a push_error. Create `test/unit/test_data_manager_bearing_off.gd` extending GutTest following the existing test_data_manager_speed_change.gd pattern: before_all loads the table; tests cover table-loads-successfully, has-all-crew-quality-grades, has-all-maneuverability-grades, at least 4 known-value lookups (regression anchors picked from the JSON), case-insensitivity for both params, and a sanity check that better crew quality (lower letter) yields >= probability than worse crew quality at the same maneuverability. Do NOT modify GameState — the autoload call to load_bearing_off_table() is deferred to its first real consumer.
tasks.verify: make test-file F=test/unit/test_data_manager_bearing_off.gd 2>&1 | grep -E 'Pass|Fail|Error' | tee /tmp/s01_t01_verify.log && grep -q 'Fail' /tmp/s01_t01_verify.log && exit 1 || true
tasks.observability_impact: Loader prints `Loaded bearing off table with N crew quality grades` on success (mirrors existing load_*_table functions). Bad-param asserts fail loudly via Godot assertion.

tasks.title: Add seed validation, fresh-seed generation, and crew_quality normalization to load_scenario (override-aware)
tasks.description: Modify `scripts/autoload/data_manager.gd::load_scenario(scenario_name)` so that after JSON parsing succeeds it (a) validates that the dict contains an integer `seed` field — missing or non-int field → `push_error("Scenario %s missing required 'seed' field" % scenario_name)` + return `{}`; (b) if `seed == -1`, generate a fresh seed via `int(Time.get_unix_time_from_system())` (cast to int from float; ensure non-negative), write it back into the returned dict, and `Trace.trace_log("ScenarioLoad", "Generated fresh seed for scenario %s" % scenario_name, fresh_seed)`; (c) otherwise `Trace.trace_log("ScenarioLoad", "Loaded scenario %s with seed" % scenario_name, scenario_dict["seed"])`. Add private helper `func _normalize_crew_quality(text: String) -> String` mapping the words used in existing scenarios to letters: "Elite"→"A", "Veteran"→"B", "Crack"→"C", "Trained"→"D", "Green"→"E", "Poor"→"F", "Demoralized"→"G". Pass-through any already-letter value (A..G, upper-cased). Push_warning + pass-through unchanged on unknown value. After seed resolution, iterate `scenario_dict["ships"]` and replace each ship's `crew_quality` with the normalized letter. Update `_create_default_scenario()` to include `"seed": -1`. Add an optional `file_path` override parameter to `load_scenario` (signature: `func load_scenario(scenario_name: String, file_path: String = "") -> Dictionary`) where empty `file_path` keeps existing behavior (build from name); this enables clean temp-file tests. Update `data/scenarios/test_basic.json` and `data/scenarios/test_fleet.json` to add `"seed": 42` at the top level (deterministic value for tests). decisions.choice: Single MovementValidator class with broken-out private methods and an internal PlottingState snapshot.
decisions.rationale: All rules consult JSON tables; GDScript favors clear procedural code over plugin-style rule engines; debugging interlocking rule failures is easier in one class with explicit method names. Rule-engine of composable rule classes considered and rejected as premature abstraction.

decisions.choice: New MovementResolver class under scripts/server/, symmetric with MovementValidator.
decisions.rationale: Clean separation between plotting (legality) and resolution (execution under simultaneity rules). ShipStateController and MovementPlottingController are the wrong concerns. Rejected: extending ShipStateController (bloats one class); method on plotting controller (session manager, not simulator).

decisions.choice: Async/await on Godot signals for contested-hex surrender and bear-off prompts during resolution.
decisions.rationale: Godot-idiomatic, single execution context, no new mini-protocol. Stub-AI prompt answers injected programmatically so deadlock is impossible in single-machine M001. Rejected: mini-session protocol (too heavy for yes/no); explicit state machine (too verbose).

decisions.choice: Impulse-by-impulse simulation: 1 MP per ship per impulse, contests checked per impulse.
decisions.rationale: Only granularity that makes contested-hex rules behave correctly in fleet engagements. Full-plot-then-contest breaks pass-through semantics between adjacent ships. Matches Close Action mechanics referenced in docs/.

decisions.choice: Stub-AI drives MovementPlottingController (handle_start_plotting, handle_select_hex, handle_submit_movement) for non-player ships, same as a remote client would.
decisions.rationale: AI plots are rule-validated; exercises the full plotting stack on AI ships; player and AI travel the same code path. Direct writes to ShipState.plotted_actions rejected because they bypass validation and would silently accept illegal AI plots.

decisions.choice: Single seeded RandomNumberGenerator on GameState; scenario JSON requires integer `seed` field; `-1` means generate a fresh seed at game start (trace-logged). EnvironmentController migrates to consume GameState.rng.
decisions.rationale: Deterministic replay for tests/debugging. Required seed makes scenarios reproducible; -1 sentinel preserves play-variability when authors want it. Single source converges existing RNG fragmentation.

decisions.choice: Resolver emits a ResolutionLog (per-impulse events + pause-points for prompts); view-side MovementResolutionPlaybackController consumes the log, animates ships hex-by-hex, surfaces prompts via signals.
decisions.rationale: Resolver stays pure-logic and fully testable. Player still gets the simultaneous-resolution drama. Decouples rule logic from animation timing. Rejected: live-animate as resolver steps (entangles concerns); instant resolution (kills drama).

decisions.choice: All JSON rule-table lookups go through typed DataManager.get_* functions with assert() parameter validation, modeled on load_movement_allowance_table() / get_movement_allowance(). Pattern: load_<table>_table() + get_<table>(typed params) + test/unit/test_data_manager_<table>.gd. Any missing wrapper is added before its consumer is written.
decisions.rationale: Single source of truth for rule lookups; consistent style; catches bad parameters fast; tables are independently testable. This is the established codebase convention; M001 makes it explicit and project-wide.

decisions.choice: Unit tests for rule math + table lookups (existing test_data_manager_* style) plus scenario-driven integration tests under test/fixtures/scenarios/ driving the full validator → resolver → state-update path. Determinism test runs the same fixture twice with the same seed and diffs the ResolutionLog. All run via `make test`.
decisions.rationale: Catches math and wiring bugs. Fixtures double as regression coverage for subsequent milestones. CLI test harness considered and rejected as premature scaffolding.

decisions.decision: Treatment of preexisting test failures during M001/S01
decisions.choice: All preexisting failing tests in `make test` (currently 45 failures across test_data_manager_tacking, test_data_manager_speed_change, test_data_manager_ships, test_data_manager_turning) must be fixed before S01 can complete. The S01 verification gate (T03) is no longer "no new regressions"; it is "make test is fully green".
decisions.rationale: User override (`.gsd/OVERRIDES.md`, 2026-05-11T22:22:15Z, applied at M001/S01/T02) changed the slice exit bar from "no regressions vs current baseline" to "all tests pass, even preexisting failures". Carrying preexisting failures forward would let the verification gate succeed on a red bar and silently accept rule-table bugs that S03+ depends on. Rejected alternatives: (a) defer preexisting failures to a later slice — defeats the override; (b) suppress/skip the failing tests — masks rule-table bugs the validator/resolver will hit.
